scope: Public-source metadata framework extending before 1 AD through human prehistory and geological deep time.
coverage_statement: Before written records, 'metadata' primarily describes archaeological, paleoenvironmental, geological, astronomical, and material evidence. It cannot represent records that never existed, and dates are often ranges derived from scientific dating methods rather than document timestamps.

domains: Pleistocene/Pliocene and earlier archaeology where applicable

provenance_rules: Separate physical evidence from later interpretation
Record uncertainty ranges rather than false precision
Distinguish original context from museum or laboratory handling
Do not infer human activity from natural geological features without supporting evidence
Do not treat absence of evidence as proof of absence
Record competing interpretations when scientific consensus is unsettled
limitations: The archaeological record is incomplete and preservation is highly selective
Many prehistoric objects and sites have unknown provenance
Ancient DNA and other biomolecular evidence may be unavailable because of degradation or sampling constraints
Dating results carry uncertainty and can be revised
Deep-time metadata is scientific observational metadata rather than human-created historical records
A global scan of all archaeological and geological metadata is not possible
security_privacy_boundary: public scientific and archival metadata only
no protected archaeological-site coordinates where disclosure could threaten preservation
status: Pre-1 AD and deep-time metadata framework added to Prev_NW.
